title: Fix invoice proration shift caused by late usage attribution to overlapping hourly windows
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Invoices are observing a systematic proration shift when late-arriving hourly usage is ingested after the per-hour aggregation job has run. The downstream billing_export job emits Stripe line items with proration amounts that do not match NetSuite allocations, causing invoice discrepancies for affected customers. Root causes suspected: watermark logic tied to run time instead of ingestion timestamp, overlapping hourly bucket assignment when usage events arrive near hour boundaries (UTC/DST edge cases), and rounding differences when converting aggregated token counts to currency units across multi-currency accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Billing export (hourly-usage-rollup) produces stable idempotent line items for late-arriving events without shifting previously exported proration amounts
NetSuite import reconciliation shows zero unexpected proration diffs for test customers across backfill and live windows
No customer-facing invoice changes after the fix for invoices older than 7 days unless explicitly backfilled and approved
Automated test coverage for watermark behavior and boundary event assignment added to the aggregation service
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created after ops reported 12 customer invoices with ~0.5% proration delta for mid-Feb invoices.

2025-02-15: Debugged pipeline: confirmed hourly_rollup cron runs at :05 UTC; late events (ingest_time > rollup_window_end but event_time <= rollup_window_end) were being appended and re-exported with a new export_id, shifting proration.

2025-02-17: Spike complete — reproduced locally with synthetic events; root cause narrowed to use of last_processed_run_time watermark instead of per-event ingest watermark for assigning 'export_bucket_key'.

2025-02-20: Implemented patch to change bucket assignment to use event_ingest_time watermark and add deterministic tie-breaker (event_id) for boundary cases; added explicit rounding-mode (bankers rounding) in currency conversion library.
2025-02-22: Deployed patch to staging, ran backfill on a 48-hour window. Observed exported line item hashes stable across replays; proration deltas reduced to <0.01% in staging reports.

2025-02-25: Engineering review: suggested adding an idempotent export signature for hourly exports (export_signature = hash(window_start, window_end, export_job_version, tenant_id)) to prevent double-applies in downstream reconciler.
2025-02-28: Preparing rollout to prod behind feature flag; coordinating with Finance for a controlled backfill policy for affected invoices.
technical_decisions: Switch bucket attribution to use ingest_timestamp when determining 'hourly' bucket assignment to prevent run-time-dependent drift
Introduce deterministic tie-breaker (event_id) for events whose ingest_timestamp exactly equals bucket boundary
Adopt bankers rounding (round-half-to-even) when converting token counts to cents to reduce systematic bias across large aggregates
Add export_signature to export records written to billing_exports table to ensure idempotency and easy deduping during NetSuite export generation
risks: Backfilling historical exports could create accounting churn if applied broadly — must coordinate Finance and support to limit to approved customers
Changing rounding mode can alter totals by a few cents across very large volumes; need sign-off from finance for accounting policy
Feature-flagged rollout must ensure compatibility with Dedicated/Private deployments that run older exporters
testing_plan: Unit tests for bucket assignment and tie-breaker logic (edge boundary and DST scenarios)
Integration test where synthetic late events are ingested and aggregation job re-run to ensure export_signature prevents duplicate line items
End-to-end staging run: full export -> Stripe dry-run -> NetSuite import sandbox -> reconciliation script to verify zero unexpected proration adjustments
Load test for aggregation job to validate no regression in latency when using ingest_timestamp checks
rollout_plan: Deploy change behind feature flag to prod ingest and aggregation services (step 1)
Enable export_signature generation in billing_export service (step 2)
Run non-destructive shadow exports for 48 hours and run reconciliation reports between new and legacy exports (step 3)
If results stable, enable dedupe-on-exporting to NetSuite for flagged tenants and run controlled backfills for customers with >$5 discrepancy after Finance sign-off (step 4)
Full enablement after 7-day observation window and manual approval from finance and legal if needed (step 5)
notes: Finance requested that any automatic backfill affecting live invoices older than 7 days be audited and require explicit approval. Support & Sales will be notified with a list of affected tenants before backfill runs.
